title: Interteam deployment gambit — choreography & safety scratchpad
summary: Working scratchpad to align product, serving-runtime, SRE, and solutions-engineering on a lightweight, repeatable choreography for small-to-medium cross-functional rollouts. Focus: minimize blast radius while getting meaningful behavioral signals (quality + latency + cost).
body:
Context and motivation:
- We run many LLM feature experiments and incremental releases; current canary workflows are inconsistent across teams and often over-index on latency without parallel signal for quality regressions.
- This doc sketches an interteam "gambit": a compact choreography that balances speed and safety for features that touch model selection, routing, or response shaping (re-rankers, prompts, tool calling).

Primary goals:
- Get early, representative quality signals within 24–72h of activation.
- Keep user-visible latency and error impact within defined SLO fraction.
- Make rollback decisions simple and evidence-based.
- Reduce operational toil: single steward per day, templated observability dashboard, automated gating where possible.

Scope (what this covers):
- Cross-team coordination for releases that change model routing, prompt templates, or scoring logic.
- Small-to-medium traffic exposures (0.1% -> 5%).
- Not intended for infra-only changes (e.g., hw upgrades) unless they affect model responses.

Key roles and language (minimal jargon):
- Steward: owner of day-to-day rollout operations (rotating). Responsible for watch, comms, handoffs.
- Model owner: owns prompts/model artifacts and quality criteria.
- Runtime/SRE: ensures capacity, autoscaling, and latency SLO observability.
- Product PM: owns hypothesis and business metrics.
- Support/CS: on-call for user escalations.

Phased choreography (compact):
1) Dry-run (local + staging): smoke tests, synthetic traffic, and automated unit quality checks (PR-level).
2) Shadow cohort (0% exposure, 48–72h): route production traffic copies to new path, collect full signals (latency, tokens, outputs). No user exposure.
3) Microcohort canary (0.1%–0.5%, 24–72h): small sampled set, prefer non-critical user segments. Collect quality evals + telemetry.
4) Guarded ramp (0.5% -> 2% -> 5%, stepwise 12–48h steps): at each step evaluate gate criteria.
5) Scale or revert (post 5% stabilization, decide to ramp to full based on product criteria).

Signals and gates (per-step):
- Safety gate: Service Errors (5xx) + latency (P95) must not exceed baseline by >X% (configurable per experiment).
- Quality gate: automatic prompt-level QA (synthetic prompts) + sampled human review (20–50 items/day).
- Cost gate: per-token cost increase must be within budget (pre-approved delta).
- Escalation gate: sudden user-reported severity or safety flags triggers immediate rollback.

Suggested numeric defaults (starter values, tweak per product):
- Microcohort: 0.2% traffic, 48h
- Step increments during ramp: 0.5% -> 2% -> 5% (12–24h per step recommended)
- Latency P95 guard: no more than +20% over baseline P95 or +150ms, whichever is smaller
- Error increase guard: +0.5% absolute OR 2x relative to baseline (whichever is triggered first)
- Quality regression tolerance: below threshold of validated metric drop (e.g., reranker nDCG delta -0.03) requires halt

A/B assignment patterns and sampling hygiene:
- Use deterministic bucketing keyed by user_id to avoid cross-day drift.
- Prefer unit of exposure = user (not request) for stateful features.
- Holdout slices: reserve critical cohorts (admins, legacy customers) from early exposure unless explicitly part of experiment.
- Synthetic replay: for any cohort, ensure we have at least N synthetic prompts that mirror top user flows for quick evals.

Observability checklist (dashboard + alerts):
- Per-cohort: request rate, P50/P95/P99 latency, error rate, tokens per request, fail mode counts.
- Quality: automated eval metric time-series, sample output diff viewer, manual review bucket.
- Business: conversion/engagement metrics that relate to hypothesis.
- Alerts: automated alert on thresholds + Slack + Pager (only for infra-level errors).
- Daily digest: steward posts summary to rollout channel with links to dashboard and critical samples.

Rollback and mitigation playbook (fast paths):
- Soft-fail: dial traffic back to previous model version (traffic switch). Keep runtimes running to maintain cache warmness.
- Hard rollback: sever new routing entirely and rollback config; issue incident if rollback fails.
- Band-aid mitigation: toggle conservative prompt/template or fallback to reranker-only path if partial regression.

Communications and stakeholder cadence:
- Pre-launch: 48h announcement to all stakeholders with hypothesis, metrics, rollback plan, steward name.
- Daily during active canary: morning snapshot + end-of-day summary by steward.
- Post ramp: one pager with outcomes, follow-ups, and lessons learned.

Simulation and rehearsal notes (important):
- Run a weekly mini-dry-run on non-critical feature to rehearse handoffs (can be automated).
- Maintain a small synthetic corpus that approximates 80% of top intents for quick QA.

Operational shortcuts and automation ideas (low effort/high ROI):
- One-click rollback button that sets routing to previous revision (with audit).
- Templated dashboard generator: input route/model -> auto build dashboard and default alerts.
- Steward checklist template (checkboxes auto-updated) to unify comms.
- Canary scheduler: wait X hours and auto-promote if gates pass, otherwise pause and ping steward.

Open questions / trade-offs to decide:
- How aggressive should default traffic steps be for large-surface features? (suggest separate track with smaller steps)
- Should we require human sampling at every canary step for model changes that affect content? (cost vs safety trade-off)
- What is our canonical quality metric per product? (need a map: product->metric)
- Do we allow feature flags to stay in prod for >30 days if the experiment is stable?

Immediate TODOs (next 2 weeks):
- [ ] Align on default numeric gates with SRE and Product (owner: Marcus)
- [ ] Prototype templated dashboard generator (owner: Elena)
- [ ] Create steward rotation schedule and pager escalation doc (owner: Aisha)
- [ ] Draft short-run playbook for external-facing customers in case of visible regressions (owner: Priya)

Notes to self / working assumptions:
- This is intentionally conservative for content-affecting changes and more permissive for UI-only experiments.
- We want to bias toward getting meaningful quality signals quickly without putting human reviewers through too much noise.
- Keep the rollout lightweight — if the change requires >2 full-day manual tasks per step it's the wrong lever.

Example quick scenario (illustrative):
- Feature: change reranker scoring to favor recency for feed.
- Dry-run: run on staging data and synthetic recency prompts.
- Shadow: 72h shadow to collect actual outputs vs control.
- Microcohort: 0.2% feed impressions for non-premium users. After 48h, see +0.8% latency P95 and minor nDCG drop (-0.01) => pass latency guard (within +20%), evaluate human samples: neutral -> ramp to 2%.

Short-term success criteria for this playbook:
- Teams run this gamed choreography without needing ad-hoc Slack threads for each step.
- Mean time to rollback under 10 minutes for traffic switches.
- Reduce manual sample review time by 30% via improved synthetic corpus and templated dashboards.

Endnotes and references:
- Keep this doc alive and short. Split detailed incident runbooks into SRE playbook space.
- If anyone wants to iterate on numeric defaults, add comments below and ping steward.

-- Marcus

notes: Informal scratchpad style. Not a finalized playbook — intended for cross-functional alignment and quick iteration. Expect follow-ups to standardize templates and automate gating where feasible.
